Design task in /opt/nxeon (Next.js 15 + Tailwind marketing site for "Nxeon", dark navy + violet theme). Give EACH product page at least one beautiful, on-brand animated "screen" that demonstrates the product working — like a mock UI/terminal/dashboard that animates in on scroll. Read components/marketing/primitives.tsx, components/marketing/Reveal.tsx, and an existing product page (e.g. app/(marketing)/vibe-coding/page.tsx already has nice mock "screens" — reuse that visual language) before building.

Build a small library of tasteful mock-screen components (e.g. components/marketing/showcase/*.tsx — a browser-chrome mock, a terminal mock, a mini dashboard/metrics mock, a mail-inbox mock, a file-manager mock) with subtle CSS/Framer-style animation (respect prefers-reduced-motion; keep it classy, not gaudy — match the existing terminal/browser mocks on the vibe-coding page). Then add one relevant animated screen to each of these product pages if it doesn't already have a strong visual: app/(marketing)/vps/page.tsx (a server/metrics dashboard mock), app/(marketing)/game-servers/page.tsx (a game control panel mock), app/(marketing)/business-email/page.tsx (a mail inbox mock), app/(marketing)/domains/page.tsx (a DNS/domain manager mock), app/(marketing)/block-storage/page.tsx (a volumes mock), app/(marketing)/features/page.tsx (Claude builder mock). vibe-coding already has screens — leave it. Keep everything self-contained (no new npm deps; pure CSS animations or the existing Reveal component). Match the existing Section/tone rhythm and don't break page metadata.

CRITICAL: Do NOT run `npm run build` or `next build` (it races with other agents on the shared .next dir). Verify ONLY with `cd /opt/nxeon && npx tsc --noEmit 2>&1 | grep -v "test/.*test.ts"` (clean for your files). Do NOT run git. Do NOT edit app/layout.tsx or any page's `metadata`. Report the components created and which pages got which screen.

## Summary

Built a self-contained library of animated mock-screen components and added a "product working" screen to every listed product page. All animations are pure CSS, gated behind Tailwind's `motion-safe:` variant so reduced-motion users see the final resting state with zero motion. No new npm deps; components are server-safe and wrapped in the existing `Reveal` for the scroll fade-in.

### New shared animation keyframes
Added to `/opt/nxeon/app/globals.css` (inside `@theme`, alongside the existing `fade-up`/`pulse-dot`): `grow-up`, `grow-x`, `eq` (live equaliser), `blink` (cursor), `sweep` (chart highlight), `line-in` (staggered rows). Each resting state equals the final visible state, so `motion-safe` degradation is graceful.

### Components created (`/opt/nxeon/components/marketing/showcase/`)
- **`Frame.tsx`** — shared `ScreenFrame` window chrome (traffic lights + title + optional pulsing "live" pill + brand aura), matching the vibe-coding terminal/browser mocks, plus a reusable animated `UsageBar`.
- **`ServerDashboard.tsx`** — VPS metrics dashboard: KPI tiles, a continuously pulsing "requests/min" equaliser with a scanning highlight, animated resource usage bars, health footer.
- **`GameControlPanel.tsx`** — game control panel: status stats, animated player-slot grid, streaming console with a blinking cursor, control buttons.
- **`MailInbox.tsx`** — branded inbox: folder rail with unread counts, message list, a freshly-arrived message that slides in, pulsing unread dots, compose button.
- **`DnsManager.tsx`** — DNS records table with typed chips, apex A-record pointing at a VPS, a newly-added TXT row that slides in with a "saved" pulse.
- **`VolumesPanel.tsx`** — block-storage volumes list with animated usage bars, mounted/detached states, monthly-cost footer.
- **`ClaudeChat.tsx`** — compact Claude builder chat: user prompt, streaming build steps that check off in sequence, live-URL result, blinking input cursor.
